scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports, from the 2026-11-23 symbol-level re-audit (method in structural-audit-2026-11-23.md).

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: Go `ExecStmt.Exec` holds a statement's pessimistic retry: `handlePessimisticDML` / `handlePessimisticLockError` re-run `buildExecutor` and `openExecutor` over the compiled `Plan` after `OnStmtRetry` (with `StmtCtx.ResetForRetry`), inside one `ExecuteStmt`. The Rust `StatementLifecycle` loop (`HandlePessimisticDml`, driven by `with_bound_statement`'s `run` closure) wraps the whole session statement instead: each attempt re-runs the statement boundary (`begin_statement_execution` / `finish_statement_execution`) and the funnel's compile (hints, binding, privilege check, `planner.Optimize`) before executing again, so no `ExecStmt` value outlives an attempt. `ExecStmt.Exec`'s `SetProcessInfo` and `observeStmtBeginForTopProfiling` are the session's (`statement_phase_observer`, `begin_statement_observation`).
